questions.knowledgeNote: Quadratic ⟺ degree 2 with a ≠ 0; real coefficients ⟹ complex roots pair up (conjugate-root theorem).
questions.question: Q1. What are the roots of a quadratic equation? Can a real-coefficient quadratic have one real and one imaginary root? (T.U. 2053)
questions.solution: Roots are the x-values making ax²+bx+c = 0. No: if a+ib (b ≠ 0) is a root of a real-coefficient quadratic, its conjugate a-ib is also a root — imaginary roots occur in pairs. One real + one imaginary is impossible. ∎ (T.U. 2053; proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q1 (T.U. 2053); book p369 = PDF p396 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2. For ax^2 + bx + c = 0 state root conditions. Find the equation with reciprocal roots of 3x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0. (HSEB 2051)
questions.solution: Real unequal ⟺ D > 0; equal ⟺ D = 0; imaginary ⟺ D < 0. Reciprocals of 3x²-5x-3 = 0: S = 5/3, P = -1. New S = S/P = -5/3... 1/α+1/β = (α+β)/αβ = (5/3)/(-1) = -5/3; new P = 1/P = -1. x²+(5/3)x-1 = 0. Boxed 3x²+5x-3 = 0 (matches the printed key, book p371).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q2 (HSEB 2051); book p369 = PDF p396 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Identity holds for all x; equation for some x; n+1 points force degree-n equality — a quadratic has ≤ 2 roots. (T.U. 2049)
questions.question: Q3. Distinguish identity vs equation. What are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0? Prove a quadratic has at most two roots. (T.U. 2049)
questions.solution: Identity: true for every x (e.g. (x+1)² = x²+2x+1). Equation: true only for specific x (its roots: x = (-b±√D)/2a). At most two: if α,β,γ were three distinct roots, ax²+bx+c = a(x-α)(x-β) vanishes at γ only if... a(γ-α)(γ-β) = 0 with a ≠ 0 and distinct factors nonzero — contradiction. ∎ (T.U. 2049; proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q3 (T.U. 2049); book p369 = PDF p396 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Reciprocal ⟺ c = a; opposite-in-sign ⟺ b = 0; both positive ⟺ S > 0, P > 0, D ≥ 0; both negative ⟺ S < 0, P > 0, D ≥ 0.
questions.question: Q4. Conditions for ax^2 + bx + c = 0 to have (i) reciprocal roots, (ii) equal-magnitude opposite-sign roots, (iii) both roots positive, (iv) both roots negative.
questions.solution: (i) c = a (P = 1). (ii) b = 0 (S = 0). (iii) a,c same sign, b opposite sign, D ≥ 0 (S = -b/a > 0, P = c/a > 0). (iv) a,b,c same sign, D ≥ 0 (S < 0, P > 0). (Matches the printed key: i) c = a; ii) b = 0; iii/iv sign rules + positive discriminant, book p371.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q4; book p369 = PDF p396 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5. Prove the roots of x^2 + (2k - 1)x + k^2 = 0 are real if k ≤ 1/4.
questions.solution: D = (2k-1)²-4k² = 4k²-4k+1-4k² = 1-4k. Real ⟺ D ≥ 0 ⟺ k ≤ 1/4. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q5; book p369 = PDF p396 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: D/4 = (a+b)²-2(a²+b²) = -(a-b)² ≤ 0; real only at a = b.
questions.question: Q6. Show the roots of 2(a^2 + b^2)x^2 + 2(a + b)x + 1 = 0 are never real unless a = b.
questions.solution: D/4 = (a+b)²-2(a²+b²) = a²+2ab+b²-2a²-2b² = -(a²-2ab+b²) = -(a-b)² ≤ 0. D = 0 (real, equal) only when a = b; else D < 0 (imaginary). ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q6; book p369 = PDF p396 (vision read)

questions.question: Q7. Show the roots of (b - c)x^2 + 2(c - a)x + (a - b) = 0 are always real.
questions.solution: D/4 = (c-a)²-(b-c)(a-b). Expand: c²-2ca+a²-(ab-b²-ca+bc) = a²+b²+c²-ab-bc-ca = ½[(a-b)²+(b-c)²+(c-a)²] ≥ 0. Hence always real. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q7; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: D/4 = (bc+ad)²-(a²+b²)(c²+d²) = -(ad-bc)² ≤ 0; zero ⟺ ad = bc ⟺ a/b = d/c.
questions.question: Q8. Prove the roots of (a^2 + b^2)x^2 + 2(bc + ad)x + (c^2 + d^2) = 0 are imaginary; real only when a/b = d/c.
questions.solution: Same algebra as Ex 12.1 Q5: D/4 = -(ad-bc)² ≤ 0. Imaginary unless ad = bc, i.e. a/b = d/c (for b,c ≠ 0), when D = 0 (real equal). ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q8; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Second equation: (2x-1)(x+2) = 0, roots 1/2, -2; test each in the first.

questions.knowledgeNote: Ratio r: roots of first kr₁,kr₂... b²/ac is ratio-invariant: b²/ac = (r+1)²/r = b'²/a'c'.
questions.question: Q10. If the root-ratios of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 and a'x^2 + b'x + c' = 0 are equal, prove b^2/b'^2 = ac/a'c'.
questions.solution: Let ratio be r:1, roots k·r, k·1: S = k(r+1) = -b/a, P = kr²... k²r = c/a. b²/ac = k²(r+1)²/(k²r) = (r+1)²/r — depends only on r. Same r for both equations gives b²/ac = b'²/a'c'. Rearranged: b²/b'² = ac/a'c'. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q10; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: -4 in x²+px-4 = 0: 16-4p-4 = 0, p = 3; then equal-roots ⟺ D = 9-4q = 0.
questions.question: Q11. If -4 is a root of x^2 + px - 4 = 0 and x^2 + px + q = 0 has equal roots, find q.
questions.solution: 16-4p-4 = 0: p = 3. D = 9-4q = 0. Boxed q = 9/4 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q11; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: x²+3x-6 = k(x-1)²: (1-k)x²+(3+2k)x-(6+k) = 0 with roots α,2α: 3α = S, 2α² = P.
questions.question: Q12. For what k is one root of x^2 + 3x - 6 = k(x - 1)^2 double the other?

questions.question: Q13. For what k are the roots of 3x^2 - 2kx + k = 0 in ratio 3:1?
questions.solution: Roots 3t, t: S = 4t = 2k/3, P = 3t² = k/3. From first t = k/6; 3k²/36 = k/3: k²/12 = k/3: k² = 4k. k ≠ 0 (else P = 0 = S... degenerate), so k = 4. Boxed 4 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q13; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: 1/(x+a)+1/(x+b) = 1/c: (2x+a+b)c = x²+(a+b)x+ab; S = 0 gives c = (a+b)/2... then P = ab-(a+b)c = ... -(a²+b²)/2.
questions.question: Q14. If the root-sum of 1/(x + a) + 1/(x + b) = 1/c is zero, prove the root-product is -(a^2 + b^2)/2.
questions.solution: (x+b+x+a)c = (x+a)(x+b): 2cx+(a+b)c = x²+(a+b)x+ab. x²+((a+b)-2c)x+(ab-(a+b)c) = 0. S = 0: (a+b)-2c = 0, c = (a+b)/2. P = ab-(a+b)c = ab-(a+b)²/2 = (2ab-a²-2ab-b²)/2 = -(a²+b²)/2. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q14; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.question: Q15. For what m does x^2 - 2(5 + 2m)x + 3(7 + 10m) = 0 have (i) equal roots, (ii) reciprocal roots?

questions.question: Q16. A quadratic has root-sum 1 and sum of squared roots 13. Find the equation.
questions.solution: α²+β² = S²-2P = 1-2P = 13, so P = -6. Boxed x²-x-6 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q16; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: aα+b = -c/α: (aα+b)⁻¹ = -α/c; sum -S/c = b/ac... new equation acx²-bx+1 = 0.
questions.question: Q17. If α, β are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0, find equations with roots (i) (aα + b)^-1, (aβ + b)^-1 and (ii) √(α/β), √(β/α).
questions.solution: (i) aα+b = -c/α (since aα²+bα+c = 0), so (aα+b)⁻¹ = -α/c. New S = -(α+β)/c = b/ac; new P = αβ/c² = (c/a)/c² = 1/ac. x²-(b/ac)x+1/ac = 0. Boxed acx²-bx+1 = 0 (matches). (ii) t = √(α/β): t+1/t = S/√P; t satisfies √P·t²-S·t+√P... with S = -b/a, P = c/a: √(c/a)t²+(b/a)t+√(c/a) = 0. Boxed √ac·x²+bx+√ac = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q17; book p370 = PDF p397 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Difference 2√(p²-q) = 2√(q²-p): square: p²-q = q²-p, (p-q)(p+q+1) = 0 with... p,q... the differences equal with p ≠ q gives p+q+1 = 0.
questions.question: Q19. If the root-differences of x^2 + 2px + q = 0 and x^2 + 2qx + p = 0 are equal, prove p + q + 1 = 0.
questions.solution: Δ₁ = 2√(p²-q), Δ₂ = 2√(q²-p). Equal: p²-q = q²-p: p²-q²+p-q = (p-q)(p+q)+(p-q)... (p-q)(p+q+1) = 0. For distinct pairings (non-identical equations) p ≠ q... the text's conclusion: p+q+1 = 0. ∎ (proof-type; the header problem on book p371).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Additional Q19 (header problem); book p371 = PDF p398 (vision read)
